articles.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has accused Washington of disrupting negotiations aimed at ending the war, while insisting that Tehran still believes a deal can be reached. articles.title: Iran’s Ghalibaf to Skip BRICS Forum in Delhi, Cites ‘Unforeseen Circumstances’ | News18
articles.description: Iran’s parliamentary speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, will not attend the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in New Delhi, with the Iranian embassy citing “unforeseen circumstances” for his absence. In a statement issued on Saturday, the embassy confirmed that Ghalibaf, speaker of Iran’s Islamic Consultative Assembly, would be unable to participate in the meeting of parliamentary speakers from BRICS member countries. An Iranian parliamentary delegation will attend the forum in his place. Despite the speaker’s absence, Tehran has reiterated its commitment to active participation in BRICS summits and meetings. The embassy said the Iranian delegation would continue dialogue and consultations with representatives of other member countries, with a focus on strengthening bilateral and multilateral cooperation, particularly in parliamentary relations.

articles.title: Terrorist Attack Rocks France: Macron's Explosive Warning After Deadly Shootout Near Paris | Watch
articles.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has condemned a deadly shooting in the Paris suburbs as a “racist terrorist attack” after one person was killed and five others were injured. The gunman allegedly opened fire from a car in Trappes and nearby La Verrière, appearing to target people of migrant origin. A 12-year-old girl is among those seriously injured. Visiting the scene, Macron said people had been targeted because of their skin colour or religion and called the incident a turning point for France. The National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office is investigating the attack, although the suspect's exact motive remains unclear.

articles.title: Delhi Metro Poster Row: Police File FIR After Anti-Government Messages Found on Airport Line | N18
articles.description: A political controversy has emerged after two anti-government posters were found pasted inside a train on Delhi Metro’s Airport Express Line. The Delhi Police has registered an FIR against unidentified persons and launched an investigation to establish who was behind the posters and the online group promoted through a QR code. The posters reportedly questioned the government’s performance and listed nine claims about changes in the country over recent years. They also included a QR code inviting passengers to join an online group, prompting investigators to examine the digital trail and identify those responsible. The case has been registered under the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Public Property Act and the Metro Railways Act. The Delhi Police Special Cell has joined the probe, with investigators looking into who pasted the material inside the train and who administers the online group linked to the QR code. n18oc_breakingnews
